heroHeadline: In Vivo CRISPR Treatment for Hereditary Angioedema Receives BLA Approval After Phase III Success
heroSubtitle: October 1, 2026: An in vivo CRISPR gene editing treatment for hereditary angioedema has cleared Phase III clinical trials and received BLA approval, marking a landmark regulatory milestone for in-body gene editing. This follows the September 30 launch of the HHS/ARPA-H SURPASS program to accelerate AI-driven gene therapy clinical trials.
footerNote: Data sourced from FDA, EMA, MHRA, NIH, peer-reviewed journals (Nature, Science, NEJM, Cell), ClinicalTrials.gov, and major science outlets. Clinical data reflects published peer-reviewed results only.
